native_result.query: What is the average length of original papers in Experimental Economics and that in Psychology?
native_result.HypoA: Studies in Experimental Economics tend to have longer original papers compared to Psychology. The average length of original papers in Experimental Economics is 28 pages, whereas in Psychology, the average is 11 pages.
native_result.HypoB: Original papers in the Experimental Economics replication project are on average 28.0 pages long (n = 18 unique originals, range 16-45), while original papers in the Psychology (RPP) project average 11.2 pages (n = 95 unique originals, range 1-31) - Experimental Economics originals are about 2.5x longer (difference 16.8 pages, Welch 95% CI 12.9-20.6, p ~ 7e-09; median ratio ~3x). Length = number of pages of the original article, not words; only projects 'ee' and 'rpp' were analysed (ml1/ml3 Many Labs and Social/Cognitive disciplines excluded). The gap is explained by publication format (economics originals are full-length AER/QJE articles with theory, appendices and econometric tables; psychology originals are short single-effect reports in PS/JPSP), plus a page-coding artifact behind a few very short RPP records. The estimate is robust to averaging over unique originals vs O/R rows (28.0 vs 11.2), to dropping the single implausible 1-page RPP record (rpp mean 11.3), and to restricting to length>2 (2.4x).
native_result.WorkflowB: pandas load of meta-regression_study_data CSV -> filter project in {ee, rpp} (115 O/R rows) -> deduplicate to unique original articles by (title, authors.o, pub_year) -> ee n=18, rpp n=95 -> per-project descriptives (mean, SD, median, IQR, range, 95% t-CI plus 10k bootstrap CI) -> Welch t-test, bootstrap CI and ratio for the ee-rpp difference -> sensitivity analyses (row-level averaging; exclude rpp.53 length=1; restrict to length>2) -> heuristic label cross-check against replication-success CSV (no joins, no length from it). Script: analysis.py; numeric log: out/analysis_log.txt
